newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Mobutu's state sector bosses suspended in new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's state sector bosses suspended in new Congo.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's government in the Democratic Republic of Congo suspended on Saturday the bosses of around 50 state enterprises appointed under ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, state radio reported.
"All the directors of public enterprises have been suspended," the radio said, adding that the minister of planning and development had signed the order.

One company director who heard the news over the radio said he was not surprised by the move which follows the arrest and interrogation of numerous former allies of Mobutu who was ousted in May by Kabila's forces after a seven-month civil war.

"I think they will shortly be appointing new directors. It is not unexpected but the big question mark now is whether the suspensions will be followed by arrests. That is what people fear," the former director of a state enterprise, who preferred to remain anonymous, told Reuters.

Jonas Mukamba, director of the state diamond company MIBA which allegedly provided vast sums of money to the private treasury of the former dictator, has been held by Kabila's alliance forces since they captured the diamond mining centre of Mbuji Mayi in April.

Numerous other former allies of Mobutu have been detained in the capital Kinshasa either in a hotel next to the information ministry or in cells across the capital. Many have also had their properties and businesses seized.

Human rights groups in the former Zaire have called on Kabila's government to investigate whether allegations of corruption and embezzlement against Mobutu's former allies follow the letter of the law. They have also described the arrests as arbitrary.

Sources at the central bank said former bank governor, Patrice Djamboleka, was arrested last weekend and was being held with other senior bank officials at the headquarters of Mobutu's much-feared former internal intelligence forces.

In a summarised version of a recent public address by Kabila in the east of the country, state television quoted him as saying he would not bow to foreign pressure to release detainees some of whom are being held incommunicado.
Kabila said the government was justified in holding them until they gave a detailed account of how the country's resources had been pillaged by Mobutu and his ruling elite.

During years of mismanagement and corruption the former dictator and many of his closest political, military and business allies, amassed vast fortunes on the back of the country's huge mineral and other resources.
When he fled in May, he left one of Africa's potentially richest countries, one of its poorest.
